title: Keep your circuit
description: Keep the circuit you built. You can come back to it later instead of starting from an empty bench.

blocks.md:
## Yours to keep

Passing the brighter-lamp experiment and the two-lamp mix saved world state under this learner’s creations folder. That circuit can sit at a bright, safe current, and it can remember a series or parallel choice. Export creation in the studio writes those files off this machine. Settings export will not include it.

This bites when you assume a reinstall or a settings backup will carry the circuit. Packs are lessons other people wrote. Your tuned loop lives with the learner until you export it.

![A loop you can keep](assets/closed-loop.svg)

```text
battery → resistor(1 Ω) → lamp → battery
bright, current 1, cap 2
```

A common mistake is treating this page as another ohms puzzle. Say why lowering resistance made the first lamp brighter, and why 0.25 was a bad idea.

blocks.promptMd: Lowering resistance made the first lamp brighter because…

choices.md: Current rose (same push, less squeeze) while staying under the cap
The lamp finally got to keep the current it had been eating
The best move was ohms 0.25 for extra power

blocks.explainMd: I ≈ cells / ohms. Ohms 1 gives I = 1, bright and safe. 0.25 gives 4 and fails the cap.

blocks.promptMd: In one sentence: why did lowering resistance make the lamp brighter, and why was 0.25 a bad idea?
